story: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price AXISBANK to move about ±5.4%, roughly 1,316 to 1,465. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 58% of the time.
AXISBANK has actually been moving about 2.03% a day this past month: on the high side for it against the past year.
Options are cheap compared with how much AXISBANK has actually been moving: they price 22.8% a year while the last month realised 32.2%.

Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap -0.3 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Puts usually cost more than this for AXISBANK: against the past year the gap is on the high side, so less fear is priced than usual.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 1,460 (+5.8% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 1,380 (-0.0%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.71; all-expiry OI PCR at the 62nd percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +1,251,875, puts +423,125 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.simple: AXISBANK futures trade 10.2 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 8.4% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
futures.analyst: Near-month basis +10.2, annualised carry 8.4% (85th percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 6.3%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Long build-up, Long unwinding, Long build-up, Long unwinding, Short build-up. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.
